title: runtime fallback graph and safety checks for heterogeneous quantized execution
creator: Asha Patel
metrics: p50 latency regression vs FP16 baseline < 10%
p99 latency under 3x of baseline during burst
accuracy degradation vs FP16 < 0.5% on calibration suite
fallback activation rate < 0.1% in steady-state for tracked workloads
description:
Goal: implement a runtime-level fallback graph and lightweight safety checks that let the serving runtime select mixed-precision execution paths (FP16 / FP8 / INT8) while ensuring accuracy and reliability guarantees. The fallback graph is a directed policy structure that defines compatible kernel sequences, permissible precision transitions, and verification hooks (quick per-request checks and periodic calibration validations).

Background: we've validated quant profiles (FP8/INT8) offline, but in production we need a deterministic, auditable way to: 1) prefer lower-cost quantized kernels, 2) detect potential accuracy regressions quickly, and 3) automatically fall back to safer precision (FP16) or alternative kernels when checks fail. This ticket covers the runtime machinery: graph representation, decision heuristics, fast per-request guards (sequence length / KV-cache hit heuristics), and an online shadow-testing flow to validate quantized path correctness over time.

Scope: implement fallback graph structure in runtime core, integrate with model calibration metadata (quant profiles), add fast safety checks (per-layer activation distribution sanity checks, output deviance thresholds), wire telemetry and alerting for fallback activations, and provide operator controls in the Console (enable/disable per-model).

Out of scope: retraining or altering quantization algorithms themselves; long-running offline calibration tooling (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes fallback graph for each model with at least FP16/FP8/INT8 nodes
Per-request safety checks run in < 0.2ms on average and correctly trigger fallback when thresholds exceeded
Shadow validation pipeline records accuracy delta for quantized path vs FP16 across the calibration suite and stores results in Dedicated dashboard
Automated canary: 0.01% of production traffic uses FP8 path in canary mode and shows <= 0.5% accuracy delta over 24h
Console toggle to opt-in/out model-level quantized routing is available and respects RBAC
qa_plan: Unit tests for graph traversal, node compatibility checks, and transition atomicity
Microbenchmarks measuring safety-check overhead across seq lengths (32/128/512)
Integration test: synthetic workloads that force fallback via injected activation anomalies
Canary run with shadow baseline collection and automated accuracy diff analysis
Load test at 10k qps to ensure fallback hot-paths do not introduce contention
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + design review; 2) Merge behind feature flag; 3) Canary with 0.01% traffic on non-critical models and collect shadow accuracy metrics; 4) Gradual ramp with monitoring thresholds (fallback rate, latency regressions); 5) Enable Console control and documentation; 6) Full rollout when metrics stable for 72h.
